text: Leoto la tshwene ya chimpanzi ratile go lekana le letsogo la yone ka bophara le boleele. Se se supa go re letsogo le dirisiwa gape go jara bokete jwa mmele wa yone fa e tsamaya ka matsogo.
eng_text: The chimpanzee's hand and foot are similar in size and length, reflecting the hand's use for bearing weight in knuckle walking.

text: Letsogo la motho le lekhutshwane go na le leoto, ka marapo a menwana a a tlhamaletseng le go feta.
eng_text: The human hand is shorter than the foot, with straighter phalanges.

text: Masaledi a marapo a diatla a dingwaga di le dimilione tse pedi go ya go dimilione tse tharo a bontsha phetogo eno mo go kgethegeng ga seatla go tloga mo go itsamaiseng go ya taolo.
eng_text: Fossil hand bones two million to three million years old reveal this shift in specialization of the hand from locomotion to manipulation.

text: Batho bangwe ba dumela go re go itemogela bontsi jwa ditoro tsa maitirelo tse di tlhaloganyesegang go ka lapisa thata.
eng_text: Some people believe that experiencing many artificially induced lucid dreams often enough can be very exhausting.

text: Lebaka le le golo la tiragalo e, ke go re ditoro tsa motho a ipona di oketsa lebaka la nako e e fa gare ga diemo tsa go robala tse di bidiwang REM.
eng_text: The main reason for this phenomenon is the result of the lucid dreams expanding the length of time between REM states.

text: E re ka o sa robale boroko jo bo kwa teng bosigo bongwe le bongwe, seemo seno sa fa o itemogela boroko jwa mmatota mme o mmele wa ga go o itharabologelwa se direga sewelo thata mo e nnang bothata.
eng_text: With fewer REMs per night, this state in which you experience actual sleep and your body recovers becomes infrequent enough to become a problem.

text: Seno ke sengwe fela se se lapisang thata jaaka e kete o ne wa tshwanelwa ke go tsoga metsotso mengwe le mengwe e le masome-a-mabedi kgotsa masome-a-mararo go bogela thelebishene.
eng_text: This is just as exhausting as if you were to wake up every twenty or thirty minutes and watch TV.

text: Matswela a ya ka go re boboko jwa ga go bo leka go lora mo go tseneletseng ga kae mo bosigong bongwe le bongwe.
eng_text: The effect is dependent on how often your brain attempts to lucidly dream per night.

text: Dilo ga di a tsamaela ka ma-Italy sentle ko Bokone ja Afrika go tswa fela ko tshimologong. Mo sebakeng sa beke Italy e sena go itlhalosa ka ntwa ka Seetebosigo a le 10, ka 1940, ma-Borithane a 11th ma-Hussar ke fa ba gapile Fort Capuzzo ko Libia.
eng_text: Things did not go well for the Italians in North Africa almost from the start. Within a week of Italy's declaration of war on June 10, 1940, the British 11th Hussars had seized Fort Capuzzo in Libya.

text: Mo tlhaselong ko bophirima jwa Bardia, ba Britain ba thopile mogolwane wa tsa bo engineer wa sesole sa Italy, General Lastucci.
eng_text: In an ambush east of Bardia, the British captured the Italian Tenth Army's Engineer-in-Chief, General Lastucci.

text: Seetebosigo a le 28, Marshal Italo Balbo, Tonakgolo wa Libya a a bileng gape e le motlhatlhami wa ga Mussolini, o ne a bolawa ke ba ga gabo fa a goroga kwa Toburk.
eng_text: On June 28, Marshal Italo Balbo, the Governor-General of Libya and apparent heir to Mussolini, was killed by friendly fire while landing in Tobruk.

text: Motshameko wa fencing wa segompieno o tshamikiwa ke batho ba maemo a a farologaneng jaaka baithuti mo yunivesithing go ya kwa go bomankge, go fitlelela kwa metshamekong ya mafatshefatshe ya di-Olimpiki.
eng_text: The modern sport of fencing is played at many levels, from students learning at a university to professional and Olympic competition.

text: Motshameko ga ntsi o tshamekiwa ke batho bale ba bedi ba lwantshana.
eng_text: The sport is primarily played in a duel format, one fencer dueling another.

text: Golf ke motshameko o batshameki ba dirisang dithobane tsa mothulo go beletsa dikgwele ka fa mesimeng.
eng_text: Golf is a game in which players use clubs to hit balls into holes.

text: Mo motshamekong wa gale, go tshamekiwa mafuti a le lesome le borobedi; motshameki mongwe le mongwe a simolola ka lefuti la ntlha, go fitlheleng a feleletsa ka la bosome-le-borobedi.
eng_text: Eighteen holes are played during a regular round, with players usually starting on the first hole on the course and finishing on the eighteenth.

text: Motshameki yo itayang thobanyane ya motshameko makgetho a a kwa tlase go ne le ba bangwe, ke ene mofenyi.
eng_text: The player who takes the fewest strokes, or swings of the club, to complete the course wins.

text: Motshameko o tshamekelwa mo tlhageng, mme tlhaga e e gaufi le mosima e kgaolwa bokhutshwane thata mme e bidiwa "ko botaleng".
eng_text: The game is played on grass, and the grass around the hole is mown shorter and called the green.

text: Gongwe mokgwa o o tlwaelegileng go gaisa wa bojanala ke se batho ba le bantsi ba se amanyang le mosepele. Bojanala ba boitapoloso.: Bojanala jwaboiketlo.
eng_text: Perhaps the most common type of tourism is what most people associate with traveling: Recreation tourism.

text: Fa ke fa batho ba etelang lefelo le le farologanyang le botshelo ba letsatsi le letsatsi go iketla le go ikhutsa mowa.
eng_text: This is when people go to a place that is very different from their regular day-to-day life to relax and have fun.

text: Mawatle, mafelo a boiketlo a nang le metshameko e e farologaneng le mabala a dikampa, gole gantsi a ngokela bajanala ba ba ratang go itapolosa.
eng_text: Beaches, theme parks and camp grounds are often the most common places frequented by recreational tourists.

text: Fa maikaelelo a moeti segolobogolo e le go etela lefelo lengwe go ka itse ka ditso le setso, mofuta o wa bojanala o itsege e le 'bojanala jwa setso'.
eng_text: If the objective of one’s visit to a particular place is to get to know its history and culture then this type of tourism is known as cultural tourism.

text: Baeti ba ka etela mafelo a a farologaneng a dikago tsa botlhokwa tsa naga nngwe e e kgethegileng kgotsa di ka tlhopha go tsepamisa mogopolo mo lefelong le le nosi.
eng_text: Tourists may visit different landmarks of a particular country or they may simply opt to focus on just one area.

text: Bakolonisi, fa ba bona tiragalo eno, le bone ba ne ba kopile thuso ya masole a a oketsegileng.
eng_text: The Colonists, seeing this activity, had also called for reinforcements.

text: Masole a a neng a thusa mo meleng ya tlhabano e e kwa pele a ne a akaretsa ba mophato wa ntlha le wa boraro wa New Hampshire wa masole a le 200, d eteletswe pele ke Mokolonele John Stark le James Reed (ka bobedi jwa bone ba ne ba nna bagenerale moragonyana).
eng_text: Troops reinforcing the forward positions included the 1st and 3rd New Hampshire regiments of 200 men, under Colonels John Stark and James Reed (both later became generals).

text: Banna ba ga Stark ba ne ba tsaya maemo a bonego bapisa legora, ka fa bokone jwa maeno a bakolone.
eng_text: Stark's men took positions along the fence on the north end of the Colonist's position.

text: Fa makhubu a a kwa tlase a bula kgoro fa Nokeng ya Mystic ntlheng ya bokone-botlhaba jwa setlhaketlhake, ba ne ba oketsa lorako ka bonako ka lobota lo lo khutshwane lwa mantswe ntlheng ya bokone fa metsi a felelang teng fa letshitshing lo lo nnye.
eng_text: When low tide opened a gap along the Mystic River along the northeast of the peninsula, they quickly extended the fence with a short stone wall to the north ending at the water's edge on a small beach.

text: Gridley kana Stark o ne a tlhoma pale sekgala se ka nna dikgato di le 100 (30m) fa pele ga legora a bo a laela go re ope a seka a hula go fitlha ba ka metlha ba e feta pele.
eng_text: Gridley or Stark placed a stake about 100 feet (30 m) in front of the fence and ordered that no one fire until the regulars passed it.

text: Leano la Amerika le ne le remeletse thata mo go thankgololweng ga ditlhaselo tse di rulagantsweng sentle go tswa matlhakoreng a a mararo a a farologaneng.
eng_text: The American plan relied on launching coordinated attacks from three different directions.

text: Mogenerale John Cadwalder o ne a tla thankgolola ntwa e e sitisang mogopolo kgatlhanong le masole a bafemedi a Borithane kwa Bordentown, e le go kganela thuso epe fela ya sesole.
eng_text: General John Cadwalder would launch a diversionary attack against the British garrison at Bordentown, in order to block off any reinforcements.

text: Mogenerale James Ewing o ne a tla ralala noka kwa Trenton Ferry ka masole a le 700, a feta a gapa borogo ja kwa godimo ga Assunpink Creek mme a thibele masole ape a mmaba go re a seka a kgona go sia.
eng_text: General James Ewing would take 700 militia across the river at Trenton Ferry, seize the bridge over the Assunpink Creek and prevent any enemy troops from escaping.

text: Setlhopha sa konokono sa masole a a tlhaselang sa banna ba le 2,400 se ne se kgabaganya noka dimmaele di le robongwe kwa bokone jwa Trenton, se bo se kgaogana go nna ditlhopha tse pedi, se sengwe ka fa tlase ga Greene mme se sengwe ka fa tlase ga Sullivan, go re se thankgolole tlhaselo ya pele bo sa.
eng_text: The main assault force of 2,400 men would cross the river nine miles north of Trenton, and then split into two groups, one under Greene and one under Sullivan, in order to launch a pre-dawn attack.

text: Ka phetogo ya boleele ja lobelo go tswa ko kotareng go ya ko sephatlong sa mmaele, lebelo ga le sa tlhole le nna botlhokwa thata, fa maatla le tiisetso e nna tsone konokono.
eng_text: With the change from the quarter to the half mile run, speed becomes of much less importance and endurance becomes an absolute necessity.

text: Ke nnete, motabogi wa maeno oa kgonang go taboga sephatlo sa maele mo metsotso ele mebedi o tshwanetse abo ana le lobele, mme boitshoko bo tshwanetse bo tlhagolelwa ka ditsela tsotlhe.
eng_text: Of course a first-class half-miler, a man who can beat two minutes, must be possessed of a fair amount of speed, but endurance must be cultivated at all hazards.

text: Bangwe ba ralala naga ba taboga ka paka ya mariga, go patagane le go itshidila mmele mo go berekanang le karolo e e kwa godimo ya mmele, e leng ipaakanyo e e siameng go gaisa ya setlha sa metabogo.
eng_text: Some cross country running during the winter, combined with gymnasium work for the upper part of the body, is the best preparation for the running season.

text: Go ja dijo tse di nang le dikotla ka bogone fela go ka seka ga dira go re o diragatse sentle, mme go ka dira go ka ama thata boitekanelo ka kakaretso jwa batsayakarolo ba metshameko ba ba saleng basha.
eng_text: Proper nutritional practices alone cannot generate elite performances, but they can significantly affect young athletes' overall wellness.

text: Go boloka tekano e e itekanetseng ya maatla, go nna le mekgwa e e berekang ya go nwa metsi, le go tlhaloganya dikarolo tse di farologaneng tsa mekgwa ya go oketsa dikotla go ka thusa batsayakarolo ba metshameko go tokafatsa tiragatso ya bone le go oketsa go itumelela ga bone motshameko ono.
eng_text: Maintaining a healthy energy balance, practicing effective hydration habits, and understanding the various aspects of supplementation practices can help athletes improve their performance and increase their enjoyment of the sport.

text: Go taboga sekgala se se mo magareng ke motshameko o o seng tlhwatlhwa-godimo fa o bapiswa le e mengwe; le fa go ntse jalo, go na le dilkgopolo tse e seng boammaruri mabapi le didiriswa tse di mmalwa tse di dirisiwang go ka tsaya karolo.
eng_text: Middle distance running is a relatively inexpensive sport; however, there are many misconceptions regarding the few pieces of equipment required to participate.

text: Dilo di ka rekwa go ya ka mo di tlhokegang ka teng, mme bontsi jwa tsone bo ka se nne le tshusumetso epe mo tiragatsong.
eng_text: Products can be purchased as needed, but most will have little or no real impact on performance.

text: Batsayakarolo ba metshameko ba ka nna ba ikutlwa e ka re ba rata setlhagiswa se se rileng le fa se sena mesola epe mo go bone.
eng_text: Athletes may feel that they prefer a product even when it provides no real benefits.

text: Athomo e ka tsewa e le nngwe ya diagi tse di botlhokwa go di gaisa dilo tsotlhe.
eng_text: The atom can be considered to be one of the fundamental building blocks of all matter.

text: Ke kgang e e raraaneng tota, e go ya ka tshwantshiso ya ga Bohr e e tlhofofaditsweng, e nang le bogare jo bo dikologilweng ke di-elekethorone tsa togwa, e e batlang e tshwana le dipolanete di dikologa letsatsi – Bona Setshwantsho sa 1.1.
eng_text: Its a very complex entity which consists, according to a simplified Bohr model, of a central nucleus orbited by electrons, somewhat similar to planets orbiting the sun - see Figure 1.1.

text: Togwa e na le dikarolo di le pedi - di-neutron le di-proton.
eng_text: The nucleus consists of two particles - neutrons and protons.

text: Di-proton di na le ngoka motlakase mme di-neutron ga di na motlakase. Di-ileketerone tsone ga di ngoke motlakase.
eng_text: Protons have a positive electric charge while neutrons have no charge. The electrons have a negative electric charge.

text: Go tlhatlhoba mogobadi, go batla o sekaseka pele go re a mme wena ga o mo diphatsheng.
eng_text: To Check the victim, you must first survey the scene to ensure your safety.

text: O tshwanetse go lemoga maemo a motswasetlhabelo fa o mo atamela le go tlhokomela matshwao ape fela a a belaetsang.
eng_text: You need to notice the victim's position as you approach him or her and any automatic red flags.

text: Fa o utlwa botlhoko o leka go thusa, o ka tswa o direla fela go dira gore dilo di nne maswe le go feta.
eng_text: If you get hurt trying to help, you may only serve to make matters worse.

text: Dipatlisiso di supa fa bolwetsi jwa kgatelelo ya maikutlo, letshogo le go feteletsa dilo go ne go tsereganya dikamano tse di fa gare ga botlhoko le bogole mo bathong ba ba bolaiwang ke mokwatla.
eng_text: The study found that depression, fear and catastrophising mediated the relationship between pain and disability in lower back pain sufferers.

text: Manokonoko a go itshosa thata, e seng khutsafalo kgotsa letshogo le le tlwaelesegileng, ke one a a neng a bakwa ke bokopano ja beke le beke jwa PA
eng_text: Only the effects of catastrophizing, not depression and fear was conditional of regular weekly structured PA sessions.

text: Bao ba tsayang karolo mo ditirong tsa ka gale ba ne ba tlhoka tshegetso e e oketsegileng mabapi le dikakanyo tse di sa siamang kaga go utlwa botlhoko ba bona dipharalogano magareng ga go utlwa botlhoko ga leruri le go sa ikutlwe sentle go go tlwaelegileng ga motsamao wa mmele.
eng_text: Those participating in regular activity required more support in terms of negative perception of pain distinguishing the differences of chronic pain and discomfort feel from normal physical movement.

text: Pono, kgotsa bokgoni jwa go bona bo ikaegile ka dikarolo tsa mmele tse di thusang go bona kgotsa matlho.
eng_text: Vision, or the ability to see depends on visual system sensory organs or eyes.

text: Matlho a bopiwa ka methale e mentsi e e harologanyeng, e e farologana ka bothata go tswa mo setsheding.
eng_text: There are many different constructions of eyes, ranging in complexity depending on the requirements of the organism.

text: Methale eo e e farologanyeng e na le bokgoni jo bo farologaneng, e farologana ka fa e amogelang dikitso ka teng mmogo le ka fa e ranolang kitso eo, mme gape e tlhoka ditsamaiso tse di farologaneng go tlhalosa dikitsiso le dinomoro ka mefuta go bereka ka namana.
eng_text: The different constructions have different capabilities, are sensitive to different wave-lengths and have differing degrees of acuity, also they require different processing to make sense of the input and different numbers to work optimally.

text: Sechaba se bopilwe ka setlhopha sa ditshidinyana tsa lesika le le le lengwe go tsa mo lefelong le le lengwe.
eng_text: A population is the collection of organisms of a particular species within a given geographic area.

text: Fa maloko otlhe a baagedi ba lefelo a tshwana ka mokgwa o o bidiwang o o ”phenotypic”, ba bidiwa gotwe ba ”monomorphic”
eng_text: When all individuals in a population are identical with regard to a particular phenotypic trait they are known as monomorphic.

text: Ha bangwe ba bone ba supa dikai tse di farologanang le tsa ba bangwe, gate ke batho ba ba iphetolang ga ntsi, mo ka teme ya seeng go tweng 'polymorphic'.
eng_text: When the individuals show several variants of a particular trait they are polymorphic.

text: Ditlhopha tsa ditshoswane le tsone di bothologela kwa di ka nang teng ka dinako tse di farologanyeng.
eng_text: Army ant colonies march and nest in different phases as well.

text: Fa ele nako ya go bothologa, masole a a ditshoswane a lala a tsamaya bosigo mme e re motshegare a ikhutse.
eng_text: In the nomadic phase, army ants march at night and stop to camp during the day.

text: Masole a simolola go bothologa fa a felelwa ke dijo. Ka nako eo, masole a aga manno a nakwana, a a agiwang sesha tsatsi le letsatsi.
eng_text: The colony begins a nomadic phase when available food has decreased. During this phase, the colony makes temporary nests that are changed everyday.

text: Megwantlo e e nna e tsaya lebaka la malatsi a tla nna 17.
eng_text: Each of these nomadic rampages or marches lasts for approximately 17 days.

text: Sele ke eng? Lefoko sele le tswa mo lefokong la Latin, "cella", le le rayang "ntlwana", mme le tlhamilwe la ntlha ke moitsaanape mongwe a sa tswa go sekaseka sebopego sa dimela.
eng_text: What is a cell? The word cell comes from the Latin word "cella", meaning "small room", and it was first coined by a microscopist observing the structure of cork.

text: Disele ke ditshika tse dinnyennye tse di leng teng mo ditsheding tsotlhe, mme ditshedi tsotlhe di dirilwe ka ele nngwe kgotsa go feta.
eng_text: The cell is the basic unit of all living things, and all organisms are composed of one or more cells.

text: Disele tsa mmele ke tsone motheo e bile di botlhokwa thata mo go ithuteng ka botshelo, mo e leng go re ga ntsi di bidiwa "Diagi tsa botshelo".
eng_text: Cells are so basic and critical to the study of life, in fact, that they are often referred to as "the building blocks of life".

text: Thulaganyo ya Methapo e boloka tiragatso ya yone ka go romela melaetsa ka methapo mo mmeleng otlhe go boloka madi a tsamaya sentle e bile a sa kgoreletsege.
eng_text: The Nervous System maintains homeostasis by sending nerve impulses through out the body to keep the flow of blood going as well as undisturbed.

text: Metlakase ya ditshika e kgona go romelwa ka bonako mo meleng, mo go thusang go sireletsa mebele mo matshosetsing.
eng_text: These nerve impulses can be sent so quickly throughout the body which helps keep the body safe from any potential threat.

text: Thoromo ya lefatshe e tlhasela thata mafelo a mannye fa o bapisa le ditiragalo tse dingwe tsa tlhago, fela di ka senya sengwe le sengwe mo tseleng.
eng_text: Tornadoes strike a small area compared to other violent storms, but they can destroy everything in their path.

text: Ditsuatsue tsa diphefo di kumola ditlhare, dikgagola dikagong, dikukela dikoloi mo phefong. Ditsuatsue tsa diphefo tse di bogale tsa bokete go gaisa tsa dipesente tse pedi di tsaya dioura di le tharo.
eng_text: Tornadoes uproot trees, rip boards from buildings, and fling cars up into the sky. The most violent two percent of tornadoes last more than three hours.

text: Sefefo se se tona se se tshosang se se na le phitlhelo ya 480km (133 m/s; 300mph).
eng_text: These monster storms have winds up to 480 km/h (133 m/s; 300 mph).

text: Batho ba tswa kgakala ba dirisa digalase tsa go bonela koteng dingwaga di le diketekete tse dintsi.
eng_text: Humans have been making and using lenses for magnification for thousands and thousands of years.

text: Le fa go ntse jalo, di-telescope tsa ntlha tsa go bontsha dinaledi di dirilwe kwa Yuropa go ela kwa bowelong jwa lekgolo la bo-16 la dingwaga.
eng_text: However, the first true telescopes were made in Europe in the late 16th century.

text: Diferekekere tse di digalase tse pedi tse amagantsweng ka tsela e e dirang go re dilo tse di kgakala di bonale di le gaufi ebile dile ditona.
eng_text: These telescopes used a combination of two lenses to make distant objects appear both nearer and larger.

text: Lefufa le bogagapa di tla tlhola di na le rona ebile ke mokgwa wa go dirisana go re fa bontsi bo bona dipoelo go tla tlhola go na le mo go gontsi go gatjwa mo nakong e khutshwane ka tsela ya bo gagapa.
eng_text: Greed and selfishness will always be with us and it is the nature of cooperation that when the majority benefit there will always be more to gain in the short term by acting selfishly

text: Gongwe, bontsi jwa batho bo tla lemoga fa go tla ba tswela mosola fa nako e ntse e ya go re ba dirisane mmogo le ba bangwe.
eng_text: Hopefully, most people will realise that their long term best option is to work together with others.

text: Bontsi jwa batho be eletsa go re motlha mongwe batho ba tla a kgona go bothologela magodimong go ya go kanoka mafatshe a mangwe, bangwe ba ipotsa go re go na leng eng koo, bangwe ba dumela go re go na le batho ba ba sa tsheleng jaaka rona kgotsa botshelo jo bongwe jo bo farologanang le jwa rona.
eng_text: Many people dream of the day when humans can travel to another star and explore other worlds, some people wonder what's out there some belive that aliens or other life may live on another plant.

text: Mme, fa seno se ka direga ga se kake sa direga ka lobaka lo lo leele. Dinaledi tse go ka tweng di sebapi di phatlaletse thata thata mo e leng go re di kgaogantswe ke sekgele sa dimaele di le di-trillion.
eng_text: But, if this ever does happen probably won't happen for a very long time. The stars are so spread out that there are trillions of miles between stars that are "neighbors".

text: Gongwe letsatsi lengwe, bana ba bana ba ga go ba tla a bo ba eme mo godimo ga lefatshe le le harologanang thata le la rona ba ipotsa dipotso ka le bagologolwane ba bone ba neng ba tshela mo go lone.
eng_text: Maybe one day, your great grandchildren will be standing atop an alien world wondering about their ancient ancestors?

text: Diphologolo di dirilwe ka disele tsa mmele tse dintsi. Di ja dilo mme di di sile ka fa teng. Bontsi jwa diphologolo di kgona go tsamaya.
eng_text: Animals are made of many cells. They eat things and digest them inside. Most animals can move.

text: Diphologolo ke tsone fela tse di nang le boboko (le fa tota e se diphologolo tsotlhe; ka sekai, jellyfish, yone ga e na boboko).
eng_text: Only animals have brains (though not even all animals do; jellyfish, for example, do not have brains).

text: Diphologolo di bonwa gongwe le gongwe mo lefatsheng. Di ikepela fa fatshe, di thuma mo mawatleng, le go fofa mo loaping.
eng_text: Animals are found all over the earth. They dig in the ground, swim in the oceans, and fly in the sky.

text: Sele ke konopo e nnyane e e fang ka botshelo mo ditshiding.
eng_text: A cell is the smallest structural and functional unit of a living (things) organism.

text: Lefoko sele le tswa mo lefokong la Selatine la "cella" le le kayang phaposi e nnye.
eng_text: Cell comes from the Latin word cella which means small room.

text: Fa o ka lebelela ditshedi ka fa tlase ga maekerosekoupu, o tla bona go re di dirilwe ka dikhutlonne tse dinnye kana dikgolokwe.
eng_text: If you look at living things under a microscope, you will see that they are made of small squares or balls.

text: Robert Hooke, moitsethutatshelo go tswa Engelane, o ne a bona dikhutlonne tse dinnye mo kgokong ka maekerosekoupu.
eng_text: Robert Hooke, a biologist from England, saw small squares in cork with a microscope.

text: Di ne di bonala jaaka diphaposi. E ne e le motho wa ntlha go lekola disele tse di suleng.
eng_text: They looked like rooms. He was the first person to observe dead cells

text: Dielemente le di kopanngwa di kgona go fetoga go tswa mo seemong se se rileng go ya go se sengwe mme di sa fetoge.
eng_text: Elements and compounds can move from one state to another and not change.

text: Gase ya naeterojene e santse e na le dintlha tse di tshwanang le tsa naeterojene ya seedi. Ya seedi e bokete thata mme dimolekhule di a tshwana.
eng_text: Nitrogen as a gas still has the same properties as liquid nitrogen. The liquid state is denser but the molecules are still the same.

text: Metsi ke sekai se sengwe. Kopanyo ya metsi e dirilwe ka athomo tse pedi tsa hydrogen le atom e le nngwe ya mowa o phepha.
eng_text: Water is another example. The compound water is made up of two hydrogen atoms and one oxygen atom.

text: A na le sebopego sa dimolekhule se se tshwanang e ka ne e le gase, seeledi, kgotsa a gatsetse.
eng_text: It has the same molecular structure whether it is a gas, liquid, or solid.

text: Le fa sebopego sa yone se ka fetoga, seemo sa yone sa khemikhale se nna se le jalo.
eng_text: Although its physical state may change, its chemical state remains the same.

text: Nako ke sengwe se se leng go re se nna sele teng; se ama sengwe le sengwe se re se dirang, mme se thata go tlhaloganngwa.
eng_text: Time is something that is all around us, and affects everything we do, yet is difficult to understand.

text: Nako e tswa kgakala e ithutwa ke ba tumelo, baitsanape ba tsa botshelo, le baithuti ba tsa maranyane dikete tsa dingwaga tse di fetileng.
eng_text: Time has been studied by religious, philosophical, and scientific scholars for thousands of years.

text: Re itemogela nako e le go tlhomagana ga ditiragalo di tswa ko isagong di fetlha ga jaana di fetela ko go tse fetileng.
eng_text: We experience time as a series of events passing from the future through the present to the past.

text: Nako e dirisiwa gape go lekanya lobaka lwa ditiragalo.
eng_text: Time is also how we compare the duration (length) of events.

text: O kgona go tshwaya go feta ga nako ka bowena ka go lebelela dilo tse di diragalelang ka go ipoeletsa kgapetsakgapetsa.
eng_text: You can mark the passing of time yourself by observing the repetition of a cyclical event. A cyclical event is something that happens again and again regularly.

text: Gompieno dikomputara di dirisiwa go fetola ditshwantsho le ditshwantsho tsa motshikinyego.
eng_text: Computers today are used to manipulate pictures and videos.

text: Ditshwantso tsa maemo a ntlha a dipopae di kgoa go dirwa ka dicomputara, ebile dipopae tsa mofuta dia oketsega mo tirisong mo sekapa ditshwantsong le mo ditshwantsong tsa motshikinyego.
eng_text: Sophisticated animations can be constructed on computers, and this kind of animation is increasingly being used in television and films.

text: Mmino ga ntsi o gatisiwa ka dikhomputara tse di tlhatlhameng go tsamaisa le go tswakanya medumo mmogo.
eng_text: Music is often recorded using sophisticated computers to process and mix sounds together.

text: Mo lobakeng lo lo leele ka dingwaga tsa bo-makgolo robabongwe le makgolo-a-mabedi a a fetileng, go ne go dumelwa fa baagi ba ntlha ba naga ya New Zealand e ne e le morafe wa ba Maori, o o neng o tsoma dinonyane tse dikgolo, tse di bidiwang di moas.
eng_text: For a long time during the nineteenth and twentieth centuries, it was believed the first inhabitants of New Zealand were the Maori people, who hunted giant birds called moas.

text: Mogopolo o, o ne wa nna le kakanyo ya go re batho ba letso la Maori ba dule go tswa mo Polynesia ba le bantsi ba leba New Zealand ba bo ba mo tsaya mo morafeng wa Moriori, ba simolola tsamaiso ya temo-thuo.
eng_text: The theory then established the idea that the Maori people migrated from Polynesia in a Great Fleet and took New Zealand from the Moriori, establishing an agricultural society.

text: Mme legale, bosupi jo bosha bo kaya fa morafe wa ma-Moriori e ne e le karolo ya morafe wa ma-Maori, ba ba neng ba sepetse go tswa ko lefathseng la New Zealand go ya ditlhakatlhakeng tsa Chatham, ba bo ba itshimolela ngwao ya bone e e pharologanyo, ya barata-kagiso.
eng_text: However, new evidence suggests that the Moriori were a group of mainland Maori who migrated from New Zealand to the Chatham Islands, developing their own distinctive, peaceful culture.

text: Go ne go na le morafe o mongwe mo ditlhakatlhakeng tsa Chatham o e neng elwe ba letso la Maori ba ba neng ba tswa ko lefatseng la New Zealand.
eng_text: There was also another tribe on the Chatham islands these were Maori who migrated away from New Zealand.

text: Ba ne ba ipitsa ma-Moriori. Go ne ga nna le dintwanyana di le mmalwa, e bo ko phelelong, ma-Moriori a bolaiwa otlhe.
eng_text: They called themselves the Moriori there were a few skirmishes and in the end, the Moriori were wiped out

text: Batho ba ba ntseng ba na le karolo dingwaga tse dintsi ba re thusitse go re re anaanele maatla le lerato la rona re ntse re batlisisa bothata le tse di padileng, puo phaa.
eng_text: Individuals who had been involved for several decades helped us appreciate our strengths and passions while candidly assessing difficulties and even failures.

text: Fa re ntse re reeditse batho ba abelana ka tsa matshelo a bone, malapa, le ka ga ditheo tsa bone, re ile ra bona boleng jwa tse di fetileng le bongwe jwa botho jo bo nang le thotloetso e e siameng kgotsa e e sa siamang ya setso sa setheo.
eng_text: While listening to individuals share their individual, family, and organizational stories, we gained valuable insight into the past and some of the personalities who influenced for good or ill the culture of the organization.

text: Le ntswa go tlhaloganya ditso tsa mongwe go sa reye go re o tlhaloganya setso, go thusa ka go lemotsha batho go re ba amana jang le ditso tsa setheo.
eng_text: While understanding one’s history does not assume understanding of culture, it does at least help people gain a sense of where they fall within the history of the organization.

text: Fa ntse a sekaseka katlego e bile o nna keletlhoko ka ditlholego, motho ka nosi le batho botlhe ba ba tsayang karolo, ba lemoga thata boleng, maitlhomo, le maatla a setheo.
eng_text: While assessing the successes and becoming aware of failures, individuals and the whole of the participating persons discover more deeply the values, mission, and driving forces of the organization.

text: Mo seemong se, a gakologelwa ditiragalo tsa maitsholo a boiperekei e bile di tlhola katlego e e thusitseng batho go re ba amogele diphetogo le ditaelo tse di ntsha tsa dikereke tsa kgaolo.
eng_text: In this instance, recalling previous instances of entrepreneurial behavior and resulting successes helped people to be open to new changes and new direction for the local church.

text: Dipolelo tse di ntseng jaana tsa katlego di fokoditse letshogo la diphetogo, ebile di tsetsekeletso ya go bona diphetogo mo nakong e e seng kgakala.
eng_text: Such success stories lessened the fears of change, while creating positive inclinations toward change in the future.

text: Go akanya le le setlhopha ke tsela nngwe e ka dirisiwang go rarabolola mathata e kopantshang dikakanyo le maitemogelo tse di farologanyeng, go bona tharabololo.
eng_text: Convergent thinking patterns are problem solving techniques that unite different ideas or fields to find a solution.

text: Tsepamo ya menagano e ke lebelo, mabaka, boikanyego le go lemoga mabaka, go dirisa dithulaganyo tse di setseng di le teng le go batlana le kitso.
eng_text: The focus of this mindset is speed, logic and accuracy, also identification of facts, reapplying existing techniques, gathering information.

text: Kgangkgolo ya tlhaloganyo ke: go na le karabo fela e le nngwe e e leng boammaruri. O akanya fela ka dikarabo tse pedi, tse di bidiwang ya nnete le e seng tsa nnete.
eng_text: The most important factor of this mindset is: there is only one correct answer. You only think of two answers, namely right or wrong.

text: Dikakanyo tse di ntseng jalo di tsamaisana le maranyane mangwe kgotsa tsamaiso e e rileng e e beilweng.
eng_text: This type of thinking is associated with certain science or standard procedures.

text: Batho ba ba nang le tlhaloganyo e ntseng jaana ba akanya sentle, ba kgona go tshwara dilo ka tlhogo ba sa lebale, go rarabolola mathata le go dira ka diteko tsa saense.
eng_text: People with this type of thinking have logical thinking, are able to memorize patterns, solve problems and work on scientific tests.

text: Mo ditshiding tsotle, batho ke bone ba ba abetsweng mo go baleng ditlhaloganyo tsa ba bangwe.
eng_text: Humans are by far the most talented species in reading the minds of others.

text: Seo se raya go re re ka kgona go akanyetsa go re batho ba bangwe ba bonadilo jang, le maikaelelo a bone, ga mmogo le ditumelo, dikitso le dikeletso tsa bone
eng_text: That means we are able to successfully predict what other humans perceive, intend, believe, know or desire.

text: Gareng ga bokgoni bo, go tlhaloganya maikaelelo a ba bangwe go botlhokwa thata. Go re letlelela gore re rarabolole go sa tlhomamang go go ka tliswang ke boitshwaro.
eng_text: Among these abilities, understanding the intention of others is crucial. It allows us to resolve possible ambiguities of physical actions.

text: Sekai, fa o ne oka bona mongwe a thuba fensetere ya koloi, o ka akanya fela go re o leka go utswa koloi ya batho.
eng_text: For example, if you were to see someone breaking a car window, you would probably assume he was trying to steal a stranger’s car.

text: O tshwanetse go lejwa ka go sele fa e le go re o ne a timeletswe ke dilotlele tsa sejanaga sa gagwe e bile e le sejanaga sa gagwe se a neng a leka go se thuba.
eng_text: He would need to be judged differently if he had lost his car keys and it was his own car that he was trying to break into.

text: MRI e berekela mo maranyaneng a a bidiwang 'nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR)', e e lemogilweng mo dingwageng tsa bo-1930 ke Felix Bloch (wa Stanford University) le Edward Purcell (wa Harvard University).
eng_text: MRI is based on a physics phenomenon called nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR), which was discovered in the 1930s by Felix Bloch (working at Stanford University) and Edward Purcell (from Harvard University).

text: Mo motshikinyegong o, maatla a magnet le marang a radio waves, a dira go re di-atom di ntshe maatlanyana a mannye a radio signals.
eng_text: In this resonance, magnetic field and radio waves cause atoms to give off tiny radio signals.

text: Ka ngwagawa 1970, Raymond Damadian, yo eleng ngaka ebile e le mmatlisisi wa tsa maranyane, o lemogile lobakala wa go dirisa ”magnetic resonance imaging” go tlhatlhobela batho malwetsi.
eng_text: In the year 1970, Raymond Damadian, a medical doctor and research scientist, discovered the basis for using magnetic resonance imaging as a tool for medical diagnosis.

text: Morago ga dingwaga di le dine phethente e ne ya ntshiwa, e e neng e le ya ntlha mo lefatsheng ya MRI.
eng_text: Four years later a patent was granted, which was the world's first patent issued in the field of MRI.

text: Ka ngwaga wa 1977, Dr. Damadian o ile a fetsa go aga sediriswa sa maranyane a "mmele otlhe" sa MRI, se a neng a se bitsa "Indomitable".
eng_text: In 1977, Dr. Damadian completed the construction of the first “whole-body” MRI scanner, which he called the ”Indomitable”.

text: Puisano e e sa direlweng gongwe e rotloetsa go re go nne le nako ya go ipatlisisa le go tsibogela batho ba bangwe.
eng_text: Asynchronous communication encourages time for reflection and reaction to others.

text: E letlelela baithuti go bereka ka nako ya bone, le go laola lobelo la tsamaiso ya dithuto.
eng_text: It allows students the ability to work at their own pace and control the pace of instructional information.

text: Go feta foo, go na le ditekanyetso tse di nnye tsa nako mme go na le kgonagalo ya go bereka ka nako e e fetofetogang. (Bremer, 1998).
eng_text: In addition, there are fewer time restrictions with the possibility of flexible working hours. (Bremer, 1998)

text: Tiriso ya Inthanete le World Wide Web e letla baithuti go ka bona tshedimosetso epe kana epe ka nako tsotlhe.
eng_text: The use of the Internet and the World Wide Web allows learners to have access to information at all times.

text: Baithuti le bone ba ka nna ba isa dipotso go barutuntshing ka nako nngwe le nngwe ya letsatsi mme ba solofela phetolo e e bofefo go na le go emela go ka nna le bokopano ba namana.
eng_text: Students can also submit questions to instructors at any time of day and expect reasonably quick responses, rather than waiting until the next face-to-face meeting.

text: Tsamaiso e ya sesha ya go ithuta e fa kgololesego e e feletseng. Ga go tsela epe e e nosi e e leng yone fela e e dirisiwang go ithuta.
eng_text: The postmodern approach to learning offers the freedom from absolutes. There is no one good way to learn.

text: Tota ebile, ga go na selo se le sosi se go ka tweng ke sone fela se se siametseng go ka ithutiwa. Thutego e diragala mo maitemogelong gareng ga moithuti le kitso e e teng.
eng_text: In fact, there is not one good thing to learn.Learning takes place in the experience between the learner and the knowledge presented.

text: Maitemogelo a rona a go itirela le go fa kitso ka go ruta batho, go ithuta ka dikgaso tsa ditshwantsho go supa yone kgang e.
eng_text: Our current experience with all the do-it-yourself and information presenting, learning-based television shows illustrates this point.

text: Bontsi jwa rona re iphitlhela re lebile lenaneo la thelebishene le le re itsiseng ka sengwe kgotsa tshedimosetso nngwe e re se kitlang re nna le seabe mo go yone kgotsa go e dirisa.
eng_text: So many of us find ourselves watching a television show that informs us of a process or experience in which we will never participate or apply that knowledge.

text: Ga re kitla re baakanya koloi, re aga phororo mo gae, kgotsa re tsaya leeto la go ya Peru go bona masaledi a bogologolo, kgotsa re fetola ntlo ya moagisane wa rona.
eng_text: We will never overhaul a car, build a fountain in our backyard, travel to Peru to examine ancient ruins, or remodel our neighbour's house.

text: Ke lebogela ba metlhale ya fibre ya ka fa tlase ga lewatle e kopanyang Europe le disatalaete tsa broadband, lefatshe la Greenland le gokegetswe sentle ka bokete jwa dipercente di le masome a borobabongwe le boraro tsa batho b aba nang le maranyane a internete.
eng_text: Thanks to undersea fiber optic cable links to Europe and broadband satellite, Greenland is well connected with 93% of the population having internet access.

text: Otela kgotsa beng ba kwa o gorogetseng teng (fa o gorogetse kwa guesthouseng kgotsa ntlong ya mong) e tla a bo e na le maranyane a WiFi kgotsa khomputara e e gokeletsweng maranyane a enthanete, mme mafelo otlhe a na le fa o ka duelang go dirisa enthanete kgotsa mafelo a sechaba a letlang tiriso ya enthanete mahala.
eng_text: Your hotel or hosts (if staying in a guesthouse or private home) will likely have wifi or an internet connected PC, and all settlements have an internet cafe or some location with public wifi.

text: Jaaka go setse go boletswe, e re ntswa lefoko "Eskimo" le santse le amogelesega kwa Amerika, go dumelwa fa le kgopisa ba le bantsi ba e seng batho ba Amerika ba ba nnang kwa kapokong ya Artic, bogolobogolo jang ba Canada.
eng_text: As mentioned above, though the word "Eskimo" remains acceptable in the United States, it is considered pejorative by many non-U.S. Arctic peoples, especially in Canada.

text: Le fa o ka utlwa lefoko leo le dirisiwa ke batho ba Greenland, ga le a tshwanela ke go dirisiwa ke batswakwa.
eng_text: While you may hear the word used by Greenlandic Natives, its use should be avoided by foreigners.

text: Banni ba sekei ba lefatshe la Greenland ba ipitsa Ma-Inuit kwa Canada le Kalaalleq (fa ba le bantsi Kalaallit), mme ba ipitsa ma-Greenland kwa Greenland.
eng_text: The native inhabitants of Greenland call themselves Inuit in Canada and Kalaalleq (plural Kalaallit), a Greenlander, in Greenland.

text: Bokebekwa, le go ilwa ga batswantle ka kakaretso, ga go itsagale gotlhe gotlhe kwa Greenland. Tota le e leng mo ditoropong, ga go na "mafelo a a kotsi."
eng_text: Crime, and ill-will toward foreigners in general, is virtually unknown in Greenland. Even in the towns, there are no "rough areas."

text: Maemo a bosa a a tsididi ke nngwe ya diphatsa tsa nnete tse ba ba sa ipaakanyang batla itemogela tsone.
eng_text: Cold weather is perhaps the only real danger the unprepared will face.

text: Fa o etela lefatshe la Greenland ka paka ya mariga (gakologelwa gore fa o ntse o tsamaela bokone, go nna tsididi le go feta), go botlhokwa go tsamaya ka diaparo tse di bothitho tse dintsi.
eng_text: If you visit Greenland during cold seasons (considering that the further north you go, the colder it will be), it is essential to bring warm enough clothing.

text: Malatsi a a maleele a selemo a ka dira go re go nne le mathata a go robala sentle le mathata a botsogo a a amanang le gone.
eng_text: The very long days in the summer can lead to problems getting sufficient sleep and associated health issues.

text: Fa go le selemo, o ele tlhoko monang o bidiwang ”Nordic”. Le ntswa o sa tshele bolweetse bope, o ngomola pelo.
eng_text: During the summer, also watch out for the Nordic mosquitoes. Although they do not transmit any diseases, they can be irritating.

text: E re le ntswa itsholelo ya San Francisco e remeletse mo bojanaleng jwa maemo a a kwa godimo, itsholelo ya yone e kabakanye.
eng_text: While San Francisco's economy is linked to it being a world-class tourist attraction, its economy is diversified.

text: Babereki ka bontsi ke ba maphata a boitseanape, a ga goromente, ba tsa madi, tsa papadi le bojanala.
eng_text: The largest employment sectors are professional services, government, finance, trade, and tourism.

text: Go supiwa thata ga yone mo mminong, mo difiliming, mo di dibukeng le ka kakaretso fela, di dirile gore toropo eno e itsege lefatshe ka bophara.
eng_text: Its frequent portrayal in music, films, literature and popular culture has helped make the city and its landmarks known throughout the world.

text: San Francisco e tlhomile mafaratlhatlha a magolo a bojanala a a akaretsang dihotele di le mmalwa, mafelo a dijo mmogo le mafelo a maemo a a kwa godimo a go tshwarelwang diphuthego mo one.
eng_text: San Francisco has developed a large tourist infrastructure with numerous hotels, restaurants, and top-notch convention facilities.

text: San Franscisco gape ke lengwe la mafelo a a botoka thata a kwa go one go nang le dijo tsa Asia ka mefuta yotlhe: tsa se-Korea, se-Thai, Se-India le Se-Japane.
eng_text: San Francisco is also one of the best places in the nation for other Asian cuisine: Korean, Thai, Indian, and Japanese.

text: Go jela nala kwa Walt Disney World go tshwana le fa o tsaya leeto le legolo la sedumedi mo go ba le bantsi kwa Amerika.
eng_text: Traveling to Walt Disney World represents a major pilgrimage for many American families.

text: Ka tlwaelo leeto le akaretsa go fofela kwa lefelong la difofane la Orlando, go tsaya bese e e yang kwa oteleleng ya Disney, go nna sebaka sa beke ntle le go tswa kwa dikagong tsa Disney, pele o boela gae.
eng_text: The "typical" visit involves flying into Orlando International Airport, busing to an on-site Disney hotel, spending about a week without leaving Disney property, and returning home.

text: Go na le ko go sa tshwaneng teng, mme ke se bontsi ja batho ba buwang ka sone fa ba re ”ba ya Disney World”.
eng_text: There are infinite variations possible, but this remains what most people mean when they talk of "going to Disney World".

text: Dithekete tse dintsi di rekisitswe ka diwebosaete tsa palabalo jaaka eBay kgotsa Craiglist ke tse di ka dirisiwang gantsi, mme di setse di simoletse go dirisiwa.
eng_text: Many tickets sold online through auction websites such as eBay or Craigslist are partially used multi-day park-hopper tickets.

text: Le fa seno se tlwaelesegile thata, se kgathanong le molao wa Disney: dithekete ga di amoganwe.
eng_text: While this is a very common activity, it is prohibited by Disney: the tickets are non-transferable.

text: Go kampa kwa lefelong le le kgakajana le Grand Canyon o tlhoka teseletso.
eng_text: Any camping below the rim in Grand Canyon requires a backcountry permit.

text: Palo diteseletso ga e ntsi thata ka maiteko a go sireletsa legope, mme di nna teng fela ka letsatsi la ntlha la kgwedi, dikgwedi tse 4 pele ga kgwedi ya go simololwa.
eng_text: Permits are limited to protect the canyon, and become available on the 1st day of the month, four months prior to the start month.

text: Ka jalo, tetla ya go kampa gope fela mo mafelong ao e simololang ka Motsheganong e nna teng ka di-1 tsa Ferikgong.
eng_text: Thus, a backcountry permit for any start date in May becomes available on 1 Jan.

text: Ka gale, dikopo tsa mafelo a a rategang thata a tshwana le Bright Angel Campground le le mabapi le Phantom Ranch, a tlala ka bonako ka tsatsi la ntlha le le buletsweng dikopo tsa peeletso.
eng_text: Space for the most popular areas, such as the Bright Angel Campground adjacent to Phantom Ranch, generally fill up by the requests received on first date they are opened to reservations.

text: Go na le palo e e lekantsweng ya diteseletso ya ba ba tsenang fela, mme ba tla thusiwa go ya ka go re go tsile mang pele.
eng_text: There are a limited number permits reserved for walk-in requests available on a first come, first served basis.

text: Go tsena mo borwa jwa Africa ka koloi, ke ngwe ya ditsela tsa go bona bontle jotlhe jwa kgaolo le go fitlhelela mafelo otlhe a seng mo mebileng e tlwaelegileng ya bajanala.
eng_text: Entering Southern Africa by car is an amazing way to see all the region's beauty as well as to get to places off the normal tourist routes.

text: Se se ka dirwa ka koloi nngwe le nngwe fa e dirisiwa ka matsetseleko mme tota go batla koloi ya 4X4 ka jaana bontsi jwa mafelo go ka gorogwa kwa go one fela ka koloi e e emetseng fa godimo ya 4X4.
eng_text: This can be done in a normal car with careful planning but a 4x4 is highly advised and many locations are only accessible with a high wheel base 4x4.

text: O gakologelwe fa o dira dithulaganyo go re e re ntswa kgaolo ya Bora jwa Afrika e tletse thitibalo ga se mafatshe otlhe a a mo tikologong a a ntseng jalo.
eng_text: Keep in mind while planning that although Southern Africa is stable not all neighboring countries are.

text: Melawana le madi a dipampiri tsa teseletso ya mosepele tsa Visa di farologana ka mafatshe e bile e laolwa ke lefatshe le o tlholegang kwa go lone.
eng_text: Visa requirements and costs vary from nation to nation and are affected by the country you come from.

text: Lefatshe lengwe le lengwe le na le melao ya lone, ya go re ke didiriswa dife tsa di bewang mo koloing tse di tlhokegang mo maemong a tshoganetso.
eng_text: Each country also has unique laws requiring what emergency items need to be in the car.

text: Victoria Falls ke toropo ka kwa karolong ya bophirima jwa Zimbabwe, boseja ga molelwane go tswa Livingstone, Zambia, gaufi le Botswana.
eng_text: Victoria Falls is a town in the western portion of Zimbabwe, across the border from Livingstone, Zambia, and near Botswana.

text: Toropo e fitlhelwa gaufi thata le di diphororo, e bile ke tsone di nang le kgogedi thata, mme lefelo leno le le itsegeng la bajanala le neela ba ba ratang go leka ditshono tse dingwe le ba ba ratang go bona tikologo ditshono tse dintsi ka nako yotlhe e batla bong ba dula teng.
eng_text: The town lies immediately next to the falls, and they are the major attraction, but this popular tourist destination offers both adventure seekers and sightseers plenty of opportunities for a longer stay.

text: Mo pakeng ya dipula (Ngwanatsele go fitlha Mopitlwe), seelo sa metsi se ya kwa godimo mme diphororo di boitshega thata.
eng_text: In the rainy season (November to March), the water volume will be higher and the Falls will be more dramatic.

text: Go papametse go re o tla koloba fa o kgabaganya borogo kgotsa fa o tsamaya mo ditseleng tse di fetang gaufi le diphororo.
eng_text: You are guaranteed to get wet if you cross the bridge or walk along the trails winding near the Falls.

text: Mo letlhakoreng le lengwe, go tla nna thata go bona bowelo jwa metsi ka ntlha ya go re metsi a mantsi thata.
eng_text: On the other hand, it is precisely because the volume of water is so high that your viewing of the actual Falls will be obscured—by all the water!

text: Phuphu ya ga Tutankhamun (KV62). KV62 e ka tswa e le yone e e itsegeng go fitisa, mo mokgacheng o - lefelo le ka 1922, Howard Carter a neng a fitlhelela lebitla le le sentseng le ise le senyege thata, la kgosi yo mmotlana yo.
eng_text: Tomb of Tutankhamun (KV62). KV62 may be the most famous of the tombs in the Valley, the scene of Howard Carter's 1922 discovery of the almost intact royal burial of the young king.

text: Ha e bapisiwa le diphopho tse dingwe, phuphu ya ga Tutankhamun ga e na boleng jwa go etelwa, ka gore e nnye fela thata ebile e na le mekgabisa e menyee.
eng_text: Compared to most of the other royal tombs, however, the tomb of Tutankhamun is barely worth visiting, being much smaller and with limited decoration.

text: Ope yo kgatlhegelang go bona ka fa setopo sa teng se sentsweng ka teng fa batho ba ne ba leka go se ntsha mo lekaseng, o tla swabisiwa ke go nne go bonala tlhogo le magetla fela.
eng_text: Anyone interested in seeing evidence of the damage to the mummy done during attempts to remove it from the coffin will be disappointed as only the head and shoulders are visible.

text: Dikhumo tse di magasigasi tsa lebitla ga di tlhole di le teng mo go lone, mme di ntsheditswe kwa Motlobong wa Ditso wa Egepeto, kwa Cairo.
eng_text: The fabulous riches of the tomb are no longer in it, but have been removed to the Egyptian Museum in Cairo.

text: Baeti ba ba se nang nako e ntsi, go botoka ba dirisa nako ya bone go sele.
eng_text: Visitors with limited time would be best to spend their time elsewhere.

text: Phnom Krom e dikhilomithara di le 12 kwa borwa-bophirima jwa Siem Reap. Tempele e, e e kwa setlhoeng sa thota e agilwe kwa bowelong jwa lekgolo la bo-9 la dingwaga, ka nako ya puso ya ga Kgosi Yasovarman.
eng_text: Phnom Krom, 12 km southwest of Siem Reap. This hilltop temple was built at the end of the 9th century, during the reign of King Yasovarman.

text: Loapi le le sa apogang la tempele, le tubego ya lecha la Tonle Sap go dira go oketsa serodumo sa go pagama thota e.
eng_text: The gloomy atmosphere of the temple and the view over the Tonle Sap lake make the climb to the hill worthwhile.

text: Mosepele wa go etela lefelo le o kgona go kopannwa fela le leoto la sekepe go ya kwa lekadibeng.
eng_text: A visit to the site can be conveniently combined with a boat trip to the lake.

text: Teseletso ya Angkor Pass e a tlhokafala fa o batla go tsena mo tempeleng e, ka jalo, netefatsa go re ga o a tlogela teseletso ya ga go ya mesepele fa o ya ko Tonle Sap.
eng_text: The Angkor Pass is needed to enter the temple so do not forget to bring your passport along when heading to Tonle Sap.

text: Jerusalem ke moshate wa Israel, le fa dinaga ka bontsi le United Nations di sa e tseye e le moshate wa Israel.
eng_text: Jerusalem is the capital and largest city of Israel, though most other countries and the United Nations do not recognize it as Israel's capital.

text: Toropokgolo ya bogologolo ya Judean Hills e na le ditso tse di kgatlhisang tsa dingwaga tse di diketekete.
eng_text: The ancient city in the Judean Hills has a fascinating history spanning thousands of years.

text: Toropo e boitshepho mo ditumelo tsa Judaism, Christianity le Islam e bile ke lefelo la tumelo, le tsa setso.
eng_text: The city is holy to the three monotheistic religions - Judaism, Christianity and Islam, and serves as a spiritual, religious, and cultural center.

text: Ka ntlha ya botlhokwa ja toropokgolo e mo tumelo ya, segolobogolo mo mafelong a mantsi a kgale a Old City, Jaresalem ke nngwe ya konokono ya mafelo a bojanala kwa Israel.
eng_text: Due to the religious significance of the city, and in particular the many sites of the Old City area, Jerusalem is one of the main tourist destinations in Israel.

text: Jerusalem e na le mafelo a ditso, dikago tsa bogologolo le tsa ditso, ga mmogo le mafelo a theko a a tlalang ka batho, mafelo a go iketla le go ja.
eng_text: Jerusalem has many historic, archeological and cultural sites, along with vibrant and crowded shopping centers, cafés, and restaurants.

text: Ecuador e batla gore baagi ba Cuba ba amogele lekwalo la taletso pele ba tsena mo Ecuador ka maemafofane a boditšhabatšhaba kgotsa mafelo a kamogelo a melelwane.
eng_text: Ecuador requires that Cuban citizens receive an invitation letter prior to entering Ecuador through international airports or frontier admission points.

text: Lekwalo leno le tshwanetse go letlelelwa semolao ke ba Lephata la Merero ya Batswantle la Ecuador, le be le fitlhelela ditlhokego tse di rileng.
eng_text: This letter must be legalized by the Ecuadorian Ministry of Foreign Affairs, and comply with certain requirements.

text: Ditlhokego tse di diretswe go neelana ka tshedimosetso ya tsa bofudugelo magareng ga dinaga tse pedi.
eng_text: These requirements are designed to provide an organized migratory flow between both countries.

text: Baagi ba Cuba ba ba nang le karata e tala ya US ba tshwanetse go etela Kantoro ya Boemedi ya Ecuador go re ba seka ba amiwa ke tlhokego eno.
eng_text: Cuban citizens who are US green card holders should visit an Ecuadorian Consulate to obtain an exemption to this requirement.

text: Lekwalo la ga go la mosepele le tshwanetse ya bo la bo letlelesegile ka dikgwedi di le 6 ka kwa ga letlha la mosepele. Tekete ya leeto la go ya le go boatla selegae le a tlhokega go supa go re o tsile go nna lobaka lo lo kae.
eng_text: Your passport must be valid for at least 6 months beyond your travel dates. A round/onward trip ticket is needed to prove the length of your stay.

text: Maeto a tlhwatlhwatlase fa batho ba itirile segopana, ka jalo fa o le mongwe kgotsa le tsala e le nngwe fela, leka go kopana le batho ba bangwe le itireng segopana sa batho ba le bane go fitlha go ba le barataro, le kgone go bona seelo se se botoka sa motho ka mongwe.
eng_text: Tours are cheaper for larger groups, so if you're by yourself or with just one friend, try to meet other people and form a group of four to six for a better per-person rate.

text: Le go le jalo, tota tota seno ga se a tshwanela go go tshwenya, ka go nne ga ntsi bajanala ba a fapanngwa go tlatsa dikoloi.
eng_text: However, this shouldn't really be off your concern, because often tourists are shuffled around to fill the cars.

text: Seno go bonala tota tota e le tsela ya go tsietsa batho go re ba dumele go re ba tshwanetse go duela madi a kwa godimo.
eng_text: It seems actually to be more a way of tricking people into believing they have to pay more.

text: Thaba e e mokgokolosa fela thata e, e gantsi e bonalang kwa morago mo dinepeng tsa matlotla a, e ntlheng ya bokone jwa Machu Picchu.
eng_text: Towering above the north end of Machu Picchu is this steep mountain, often the backdrop to many photos of the ruins.

text: Go bonala go le bokete go tswa kwa tlase, mme go motlhotlogelo e bile go thata go ya kwa godimo, mme gone bontsi jwa batho ba ka selekanyo se se rileng ba itekanetseng ba tshwanetse ba kgona go palamela koo ka metsotso e ka nna 45.
eng_text: It looks a bit daunting from below, and it is a steep and difficult ascent, but most reasonably fit persons should be able to make it in about 45 minutes.

text: Mantswe a go gatiwang mo go one a beilwe mo bontsing jwa tsela ya teng, mme mo dikarolong tse di tlhatlogelelang thata tsa megala ya tshipi di neelana ka tshegetso ya matshwaro a diatla.
eng_text: Stone steps are laid along most of the path, and in the steeper sections steel cables provide a supporting handrail.

text: Ka go rialo, solofela go felelwa ke mowa, mme o itlhokomele mo dikarolong tse di motlhatlogo thata, segolobogolo jang fa go le metsi, e re ka go ka nna kotsi ka bonako.
eng_text: That said, expect to be out of breath, and take care in the steeper portions, especially when wet, as it can become dangerous quickly.

text: Go na le logaga lo lo nnye gaufi le kwa setlhoeng se o tshwanetse go feta ka sone, le kwa tlase thata mme e bile ka le pitlagane thata o tshwanelwa ke go ipateletsa tota go tsena mo go lone.
eng_text: There's a tiny cave near the top that must be passed through, it is quite low and a rather tight squeeze.

text: Go bona mafelo le diphologolo tsa naga tsa Galapagos go bonala botoka go gaisa fa o dirisa mokoro, fela jaaka Charles Darwin a ile a dira ka 1835.
eng_text: Seeing the sites and wildlife of the Galapagos is best done by boat, just as Charles Darwin did it in 1835.

text: Dikepe tse dikgolo tsa loeto lwa go ijesa monate di ka nna 60 di tsamaya ka metlha kwa Galapagos – go tswa go selekanyo sa bapalami ba le 8 go ya go ba le 100.
eng_text: Over 60 cruise ships ply the Galapagos waters - ranging in size from 8 to 100 passengers.

text: Bontsi jwa batho ba kopa ba ipeela sebaka go sale gale thata (e re ka dikepe ga ntsi di tlala ka paka ya fa di palangwa thata).
eng_text: Most people book their place well in advance (as the boats are usually full during the high season).

text: Netefatsa gore modiredii yo o bukang mo go ene ke moitsaanape wa Galapagos yo o nang le kitso e e tseneletseng ka mefuta ya dikepe tse di farologaneng.
eng_text: Be sure the agent through whom you book is a Galapagos specialist with a good knowledge of a wide variety of ships.

text: Se se tla netefatsa go re dikeletso tsa ga go lekana dikgwetlho ka go kgethega di nyalanywa le sekepe se se a tshwanelang.
eng_text: This will ensure that your particular interests and/or constraints are matched with the ship most suitable to them.

text: Pele ga ba-Spain ba goroga mo lekgolong la bo-16 la dingwaga, Chile e e kwa bokone e ne e busiwa ke Inca fa batho ba ba tlholegang kwa Araucania (Mapuche) ba ne ba nna mo bogareng le borwa jwa Chile.
eng_text: Before the Spanish arrived in the 16th century, northern Chile was under Inca rule while the indigenous Araucanians (Mapuche) inhabited central and southern Chile.

text: Morafe wa Mapuche o ne gape e le o mongwe wa merafe e e tlholegileng kwa Amerika mme ya ikemela ka bo yone, e e neng e sa tsenngwa ka botlalo mo pusong ya ba ba buang se-Spanish go fitlhela fa Chile e se na go ikemela ka bo yone.
eng_text: The Mapuche were also one of the last independent American indigenous groups, that were not fully absorbed into Spanish-speaking rule until after Chile's independence.

text: Le fa Chile e nnile le boipuso ka 1810 (mo gare ga dintwa tsa Napoleon tse di tlogetseng Spain e sena puso ya bogareng e e berekang ka dingwaga di le mmalwa), go fenngwa go go feletseng ga ba-Spain ga go a ka ga fitlhelelwa go fitlha ka 1818.
eng_text: Although Chile declared independence in 1810 (amid the Napoleonic wars that left Spain without a functioning central government for a couple of years), decisive victory over the Spanish was not achieved until 1818.

text: Rephaboliki ya Dominican (ka se-Spain: República Dominicana) ke naga ya Caribbean e e fitlhelwang kwa sephatlong sa botlhaba jwa setlhaketlhake sa Hispaniola, e e e aroganang le Haiti.
eng_text: The Dominican Republic (Spanish: República Dominicana) is a Caribbean country that occupies the eastern half of the island of Hispaniola, which it shares with Haiti

text: Ntle le motlhaba o mosweu wa mo letshitshing le lefatshe le le dithaba, naga eno ke legae la toropo ya bogologolo ya Yuropa kwa Amerika, e gompieno e leng karolo ya Santo Domingo.
eng_text: Besides white sand beaches and mountain landscapes, the country is home to the oldest European city in the Americas, now part of Santo Domingo.

text: Setlhakatlhake se ne pele se nniwa ke ba-Taino le ba-Caribe. Ba-Caribe e ne e le batho ba puo ya se-Arawakan ba ba gororileng ka mo e ka nnang 10,000 BCE.
eng_text: The island was first inhabited by the Taínos and Caribes. The Caribes were an Arawakan-speaking people who had arrived around 10,000 BCE.

text: Mo dingwageng di le mmalwanyana fela morago ga go re babatlisisi ba Yuropa ba goroge, baagi ba ba-Taino ba ne ba fokoditse thata ke bathopi ba ba-Spain.
eng_text: Within a few short years following the arrival of European explorers, the population of Tainos had significantly been reduced by the Spanish conquerors

text: Go ya ka Fray Bartolomé de las Casas (Tratado de las Indias) magareng a 1492 le 1498 bathopi ba ba-Spain ba ile ba bolaya ba-Taino ba ka nna 100,000.
eng_text: Based on Fray Bartolomé de las Casas (Tratado de las Indias) between 1492 and 1498 the Spanish conquerors killed around 100,000 Taínos.

text: Jardin de la Unión. Sebaka seno se ne sa agiwa go nna holo ya baitlami mo lekgolong la bo-17 la dingwaga, e ga jaana Templo de San Diego e leng yone fela kago e e santseng e le gone.
eng_text: Jardín de la Unión. This space was built as the atrium for a 17th-century convent, of which the Templo de San Diego is the sole surviving building.

text: Ga jaana e dirisiwa jaaka marekelo a konokono, mme e nna e na le dilo di le dintsi tse di diragalang mo go yone, motshegare le bosigo.
eng_text: It now functions as the central plaza, and always has a lot of things going on, day and night.

text: Go nale mafelo a le mantsi a go ja a a dikaganyeditseng tshingwana, e bile ka thapama le maitseboa ditiragatso koo gantsi di direrelwa ka fa tlase ga moriti wa sekgele.
eng_text: There are a number of restaurants surrounding the garden, and in the afternoons and evening there free concerts are often given from the central gazebo.

text: Callejon del Beso (Mogogoro wa Tladimothwana). Mathudi a le mabedi a a kgaogantsweng ke disenthimithara di le 69 fela ke legae la mogaka wa bogologolo wa marato.
eng_text: Callejon del Beso (Alley of the Kiss). Two balconies separated by only 69 centimeters is home of an old love legend.

text: Ka dipeni di le mmalwanyana fela bana bangwe ba ka go tlotlela kgang ya teng.
eng_text: For a few pennies some children will tell you the story.

text: Bowen Island ke mosepele wa letsatsi o o ratiwang thata kgotsa go intsha ga mafelobeke go ya go palama mokorwana wa kaya, go haeka, mabenkele, mafelo a go ja, le tse dingwe tse dintsi.
eng_text: Bowen Island is a popular day trip or weekend excursion offering kayaking, hiking, shops, restaurants, and more.

text: Batho bano ba reetsang ka kelotlhoko ba fitlhelwa kwa Howe Sound ka fa ntle fela ga Vancouver, mme go motlhofo go e etela ka dipalamo tsa sechaba tsa mo metsing tse di tswang kwa Setlhaketlhakeng sa Granville mo toropokgolong ya Vancouver.
eng_text: This authentic community is located in Howe Sound just off Vancouver, and is easily accessed via scheduled water taxis departing Granville Island in downtown Vancouver.

text: Go bao ba ratang metshameko ya kwa ntle, tsela ya kwa godimo kwa Lewatleng go ya mankalenkaleng a Loapi e botlhokwa thata.
eng_text: For those who enjoy outdoor activities, a trek up the Sea to Sky corridor is essential.

text: Whistler (sekgala sa ura le sephatlo o kgweetsa go tswa kwa Vancouver), e a tura mme e itsege thata ka ntlha ya metshameko ya Olimpiki ya Mariga ya 2010.
eng_text: Whistler (1.5 hour drive from Vancouver) is expensive but well-known because of the 2010 Winter Olympics.

text: Mo marigeng, o ka rata bontsi jwa metshameko ya skiing kwa bokone jwa America, ka selemo o leke go pagama dithaba gwa boammaruri.
eng_text: In the winter, enjoy some of the best skiing in North America, and in the summer try some authentic mountain biking.

text: Tetlelelo e tshwanetswe ya kopiwa nako e sale teng. O tshwanetse wa bo o na le tetlelelo ya go lala kwa Sirena.
eng_text: Permits must be reserved in advance. You must have a permit to stay overnight at Sirena.

text: Sirena ke yone fela lefelo la batlhokomedi ba paraka le le neelanang ka lefelo la boroko le dijo tse di bolelo mo godimo ga go kampa. La Leona, San Pedrillo, le Los Patos tsone di neelana fala ka go kampa go sena dijo.
eng_text: Sirena is the only ranger station that offers dormitory lodging and hot meals in addition to camping. La Leona, San Pedrillo, and Los Patos offer only camping with no food service.

text: Go a kgonagala go bona teseletso ya phaka gotswa go mannong a batlhokomedi kwa Puerto Jiménez, mme ga ba tseye dikarata tsa madi.
eng_text: It is possible to secure park permits directly from the Ranger Station in Puerto Jiménez, but they do not accept credit cards

text: Ba Tirelo ya Diparaka (MINAE) ga ba neelane ka ditetlelelo tsa paraka ka sebaka sa kgwedi e le nngwe go sale gale ka nako e go goroga go lebeletsweng ka yone.
eng_text: The Park Service (MINAE) does not issue park permits more than one month in advance of anticipated arrival.

text: CafeNet El Sol e neelana ka tirelo e e beeleditsweng ka didolara tsa Amerika di le masome a mararo, US$30, kgotsa di le lesome, $10 ya go tsena ya letsatsi lotlhe. Dintlha ka botlalo di mo letlakaleng la webosaete ya bone ya Corcovado.
eng_text: CafeNet El Sol offers a reservation service for a fee of US$30, or $10 for one-day passes; details on their Corcovado page.

text: Ditlhaketlhake tsa Cook ke naga ya ditlhaketlhake tse di sa kopaneng ka gope le New Zealand, e e fitlhelwang kwa Polynesia, e e kwa bogareng jwa Borwa jwa Lewatle la Pacific.
eng_text: The Cook Islands are an island country in free association with New Zealand, located in Polynesia, in the middle of the South Pacific Ocean.

text: Ke ditlhopha tsa ditlhaketlhake tse lesome le botlhano tse di anameng bophara le boleele jwa dikhilomitara di le dimilione 2.2 mo lewatleng.
eng_text: It is an archipelago with 15 islands spread out over 2.2 million km2 of ocean.

text: E re ka di na le nako e e tshwanang le ya Hawaii, ditlhaketlhake tse ka nako tse dingwe di tsewa e le "Hawaii ke Australia le New Zealand".
eng_text: With the same time zone as Hawaii, the islands are sometimes thought of as "Hawaii down under".

text: Le fa e le nnye, e gakolola baeti bangwe ba bagodi ka fa Hawaii e neng e le ka teng pele a nna leloko la Amerika - go se na dihotele tse ditona tsa bajanala le ditlhabologo tse dingwe.
eng_text: Though smaller, it reminds some elderly visitors of Hawaii before statehood without all the large tourist hotels and other development.

text: Ditlhaketlhake tsa Cook ga di na toropo dipe mme di dirilwe ka ditlhaketlhake di le 15 tse di farologaneng. Ditlhaketlhake tsa konokono ke Rarotonga le Aitukaki.
eng_text: The Cook Islands do not have any cities but are composed of 15 different islands. The main ones are Rarotonga and Aitutaki.

text: Mo mafatsheng a a tlhabologileng gompieno, go gweba ka go fa batho boroko jwa bed-and-breakfast ja maemo a a ko godimo, go tseelwa ko go dimo fela thata ke bang ba mafelo a teng.
eng_text: In developed countries today, providing deluxe bed and breakfasts has been raised to a sort of art-form.

text: Fa go lebilwe maroko a madi a a kwa godimo, mafelo a di-B&B a phadisanya thata ka dilo tse pedi: boleng jwa dikobo le dijo tsa mo mosong.
eng_text: At the top end, B&Bs obviously compete mainly on two main things: bedding and breakfast.

text: Ka tshwanelo, kwa mafelong a maemo a a kwa godimo, o ka fithela malao a alotsweng ka mabaibai - gongwe kojwana e e rokilweng ka diatla; kgotsa bolao jwa boleng jo bo kwa godimo, jo bo dirilweng bogologolo.
eng_text: Accordingly, at the finest such establishments one is apt to find the most luxurious bedding, maybe a handmade quilt or an antique bed.

text: Difitlholo di akaretsa dijo tse di monate tsa setlha se se rileng tsa kgaolo kgotsa sejo sa molaletsi se se kgethegileng.
eng_text: Breakfast may include seasonal delights of the region or the host's speciality dish.

text: Setheo e katswa e le kago ya bogologolo e na le didirisiwa tse dintle tsa bogologolo, e nale ditlhare tse dintle tse di tlhokomelwang, le lefelo la go thuma.
eng_text: The setting might be an historic old building with antique furnishings, manicured grounds and a swimming pool.

text: Go tsena mo koloing ya ga go o bo o tsaya loeto lo lo leele go itumedisa thata ka go sa tsenye dingalo.
eng_text: Getting into your own car and heading off on a long road trip has an intrinsic appeal in its simplicity.

text: Fa o tshwantshanya dikoloi tse dikgolwane le ya ga go, o tshwanetse o bo o tlwaetse go kgweetsa ya ga go mme e bile o itse makowa a yone.
eng_text: Unlike larger vehicles, you are probably already familiar with driving your car and know its limitations.

text: Go tlhoma tente mo lelwapeng la mong kgotsa toropo go sa kgathalesege go re e botona bo kae go kgona go go biletsa dira.
eng_text: Setting up a tent on private property or in a town of any size can easily attract unwanted attention.

text: Ka bokhutshwana go dirisa koloi ya gago go tsaya loeto lwa koloi go siame, mme gase tsela e e siametseng go kampa.
eng_text: In short, using your car is a great way to take a road trip but seldom in itself a way to "camp".

text: O ka kampa mo koloing fa o na le bene e tona, koloi ya modiro wa SUV, sedan kgotsa Station Wagon e e nang le ditilo tse o kgonang go di robatsa.
eng_text: Car camping is possible if you have a large minivan, SUV, Sedan or Station Wagon with seats that lay down.

text: Di-hotele tse dingwe di na le ditso tsa go tsweng ko nakong ya letlepu, ya go sentse go dirisiwa diterena le dikepe tsa mosi wa metsi; pele ga ntwa ya lefatshe ya bobedi, mo dingwageng tsa bo-18, le tsa bo-19 di simologa.
eng_text: Some hotels have a heritage from the golden age of steam railways and ocean liners; before the Second World War, in the 19th or early 20th centuries.

text: Diotela tse ke kwa go tsone go neng go nna bahumi le batho ba ba itsegeng thata ba nako eo, mme e bile go le ga ntsi di rekisa dijo tsa maemo a a kwa godimo gape di na le mafelo a maitiso a a haphegileng.
eng_text: These hotels were where the rich and the famous of the day would stay, and often had fine dining and nightlife.

text: Mekgabisa ya bogologolo, letlhoko la ditlamelo tsa sesha, le go bo e le tsa dinako tsele tsotlhe ke dingwe tsa dilo tse di dirang go re di nne dintle le go feta.
eng_text: The old fashioned fittings, the lack of the latest amenities, and a certain graceful agedness are also part of their character.

text: E re ntswa ka gale e le tsa beng, di a tle di dirisiwe ke baeteledipele le batlotlegi ba bangwe.
eng_text: While they are usually privately owned, they sometimes accommodate visiting heads of state and other dignitaries.

text: Mojanala yo o nang le madi a sisimosang o ka sekaseka go dikologa lefatshe a ijesa monate, a eta a ikhutsa ka go etela bontsi kwa diotela tseno.
eng_text: A traveller with piles of money might consider a round the world flight, broken up with stays in many of these hotels.

text: Maharathatha a bojanala ke lekgotla le le kopanyang bajanala le benggae mo ditoropong tse ba di etelang.
eng_text: A hospitality exchange network is the organization that connects travelers with locals in the cities they are going to visit.

text: Go tsenelela mokgatlo yo gantsi go tlhokana le go re o tlatse fomo mo enthaneteng; le fa ntswa fa gongwe go ka thokana le go rurifatsa itshupo ya gago go feta foo.
eng_text: Joining such a network usually just requires filling out an online form; although some networks offer or require additional verification.

text: Go tswa foo, bajanala ba neelwa mekwalo ya pampiri kgotsa e e mo mafaratlhatlheng a enthanete, fa gongwe e patilwe ke bopaki kwa bajanala ba bangwe.
eng_text: A listing of available hosts is then provided either in print and/or online, sometimes with references and reviews by other travelers.

text: Mothale wa Couchsurfing o tlhamilwe ka Hirikgong ka 2004 rramaranyane wa dikhomputara Casey Fenton a sena go bona sefofane sa madi a a kwa tlase go ya Iceland mme a sena kwa a ka bayang tlhogo teng.
eng_text: Couchsurfing was founded in January 2004 after computer programmer Casey Fenton found a cheap flight to Iceland but did not have a place to stay.

text: O romeletse baithuti ba yunibestithi e e gaufi molaetsa wa email, mme a amogela diphetolo tse dintsi thata, e le tsa batho ba ba reng ba ka mo fa boroko ja mahala.
eng_text: He emailed students at the local university and received an overwhelming number of offers for free accommodation.

text: Dihosetele thata di lebantswe banana - ba ga ntsi e leng batho ba dingwaga tse di masome a mabedi go ya kwa go a a kwa tlase ga a masome marataro - mme go ga ntsi bajanala ba bagolwane ba fitlhelwa koo.
eng_text: Hostels cater primarily to young people – a typical guest is in their twenties – but you can often find older travellers there too.

text: Malapa a a nang le bana a ga a tlwaelesega, mme go na le dihosetele tse dingwe tse di kgonang go ba fa boroko mo matlong a a sa kopanelwang.
eng_text: Families with children are a rare sight, but some hostels do allow them in private rooms.

text: Toropokgolo ya China, Beijing e tla tshegetsa metshameko ya Olympics Winter Games ka 2022. Se se tla dira toropo e yone ya ntlha go tshegetsa metshameko ya Olympics ka mariga le selemo.
eng_text: The city of Beijing in China will be the host city of the Olympic Winter Games in 2022, which will make it the first city to have hosted both the summer and winter Olympics.

text: Mokete ya pulo le wa go tswalelwa ga metshameko ya ”Indoor Ice Events” e tla tshwarelwa ko Beijing.
eng_text: Beijing will host the opening and closing ceremonies and the indoor ice events.

text: Ditiragalo tse dingwe tsa go relela mo serameng (skiing) di tla tshwarelwa kwa lefelong la itheletsho mo serameng la Taizicheng kwa Zhangjiakou, le le dikhilomithara tse makgolo a mabedi le masome mabedi (dimmaele tse di lekgolo le masome nane) go tswa Beijing.
eng_text: Other skiing events will be at the Taizicheng ski area in Zhangjiakou, about 220 km (140 miles) from Beijing.

text: Bontsi jwa ditempele di na le moletlo wa Ngwaga le Ngwaga o o simololang fa Ngwanatsele a fela go fitlha Motsheganong ele fa gare, mme e farologana go ya ka khalendara ya ngwaga ya tempele nngwe le nngwe.
eng_text: Most of the temples do have an Annual festival starting from November end to Mid of May, which varies according to each temple's annual calendar.

text: Bontsi jwa meletlo ya tempele bo dirwa ele bontlhabongwe jwa segopotso sa tempele, letsatsi la matsalo la modingwana yo ka nako eo a ikametseng tempele kgotsa moletlo mongwe le mongwe fela o o amanang le tempele.
eng_text: Most of the temple festivals is celebrated as part of temple's anniversary or presiding deity's birthday or any other major event associated with the temple.

text: Meletlo ya ditempele tsa Kerala e kgatlha fela thata, go etle go bonagale gape le ditlou tsedi kgabisitsweng, baopedi ba kereke letse dingwe.
eng_text: Kerala's temple festivals are very interesting to see, with regular procession of decorated elephants, temple orchestra and other festivities.

text: Dipontsho tsa Lefatshe (tse ga ntsi di bidiwang World Exposition, kgotsa fela Expo) ke moletlo o mogolo wa bodichabachaba wa botaki le maranyane.
eng_text: A World's Fair (commonly called World Exposition, or simply Expo) is large international festival of arts and sciences.

text: Dinaga di dira ditshupetso tsa botaki le dithuto mo pavilion ya naga, go supa dikgwetlho tsa lefatshe, le ka fa dilo di dirwang ka teng mo ditsong tsa one.
eng_text: Participating countries present artistic and educational displays in national pavilions to showcase world issues or their country's culture and history.

text: Dipontsho tsa Bodichabachaba tsa Temo ke ditiragalo tse di kgethegileng tse di bontshang dithunya, ditshingwaga tsa temo le sepe fela se se amanang le dijalo.
eng_text: International Horticultural Expositions are specialised events which showcase floral displays, botanical gardens and anything else to do with plants.

text: Le fa go twe di diragala ngwaga nngwe le nngwe (fela fa e le go re di mo mafatsheng a farologanyeng), mo nneteng ga go direge jalo.
eng_text: Although in theory they can take place annually (so long as they are in different countries), in practice they are not.

text: Meletlo eno gantsi e tsaya lobaka lwa dikgwedi tse tharo go fitlha go tse thataro, mme e tshwarelwa mo mafelong a a fetang diheketara di le 50.
eng_text: These events normally last anywhere between three and six months, and are held on sites no smaller than 50 hectares.

text: Go na le mefuta e e farologaneng ya difilimi e e dirisitsweng mo dingwageng tse di fetileng. Filimi tsa go tlwaelegatsa tsa 35 mm (ya negative ya 36 ka 24mm) ke tsone tse di itseweng thata.
eng_text: There are many different film formats that have been used over the years. Standard 35 mm film (36 by 24 mm negative) is much the commonest.

text: Gantsi e ka emisediwa motlhofo tota fa o ka felelwa, mme e naya resolushene e e sa tlhomamang fa e bapisiwa le khamera ya ga jaana ya dijithale ya lense e le nngwe.
eng_text: It can usually be replenished fairly easily if you run out, and gives resolution roughly comparable to a current DSLR.

text: Dikhamera tsa selekanyo se se mo maemong a a fa gare di dirisa selekanyo sa 6cm ka 6cm go tlhomamisa thata e le 56 ka 56mm o o bonalang ka tsela e e farologaneng.
eng_text: Some medium-format film cameras use a 6 by 6 cm format, more precisely a 56 by 56 mm negative.

text: E supegetsa botoka go ka nna gane go feta ya 35mm (3136 mm2 kgatlhanong le 684).
eng_text: This gives resolution almost four times that of a 35 mm negative (3136 mm2 versus 864).

text: Go tsaya diphologolo dinepe ke nngwe ya botaki jo bo nang le dikgwetlho tse dintsi. Go tlhokana le dilo tse di tshwanang le go nna lesego, bopelotele, maitemogelo le didiriswa tsa maemo a a kwa godimo.
eng_text: Wildlife is among the most challenging motifs for a photographer, and needs a combination of good luck, patience, experience and good equipment.

text: Go le ga ntsi batho ba tsaya motlhofo go tsaya diphologolo dinepe, mme fela jaaka go tsaya dinepe ka kakaretso, senepe se kgona go senola dilo tse dintsi thata.
eng_text: Wildlife photography is often taken for granted, but like photography in general, a picture is worth a thousand words.

text: Go tsaya ditshwantsho tsa diphologolo tsa naga go tlhoka lense ya taolabogolo e telele; fela dilo di tshwana le letsomane la dinonyane kgotsa setshedi se se nnye se tlhoka lense tse dingwe.
eng_text: Wildlife photography often requires a long telephoto lens, though things like a flock of birds or a tiny creature need other lenses.

text: Go thata go bona diphologolo tse dintsi tse di sa tlwaelegang, mme ka dinako dingwe diphaka di na le melao ka go tsaya ditshwantsho ka mabaka a kgwebo.
eng_text: Many exotic animals are hard to find, and parks sometimes have rules about taking photographs for commercial purposes.

text: Diphologolo tse di tlhaga di ka tswa di le ditlhong kgotsa di le dikgoka. Seemo se ka nna tsididi, mogote kgotsa go seng jalo, se se tletseng letlhoo.
eng_text: Wild animals might either be shy or aggressive. The environment might be cold, hot, or otherwise hostile.

text: Lefatshe ka bophara le na le dipuo tse di fetang 5, 000, go balelwa tse di fetang masome a mabedi tse di buiwang ke batho ba le 50 million kgotsa go feta.
eng_text: The world has over 5,000 different languages, including more than twenty with 50 million or more speakers.

text: Gape, go le ga ntsi go motlhofo go tlhaloganya mafoko a a kwadilweng botoka go na le a a buiwang. Go ntse jalo segolobogolo fa go tla mo diatereseng ka ga ntsi go le bokete go a bua sentle.
